quote.text: No thefts of free will reported.”[—Epictetus.]
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Recognize that each child is born with an innate freedom of will; nurture their ability to choose wisely and act with integrity by modeling ethical behavior and respectful decision-making.
    • Encourage open dialogue and independent thinking, reassuring them that no external force can steal their inner power, as their choices and values are uniquely theirs to develop.
  • Leadership
    • Lead by example by respecting and fostering the free will of your team; true leadership lies in empowering others to make decisions that reflect their values and strengths.
    • In times of challenge, remind your team that no one can strip away their autonomy; resilience and integrity are maintained when each individual remains true to their personal sense of purpose.
  • Product Management
    • Design products that honor user autonomy by providing clear choices and intuitive interfaces, ensuring that customers feel empowered rather than manipulated.
    • Adopt a mindset where every feature is developed to serve and enhance user freedom, reinforcing trust and genuine engagement with the product.
